name: Addons are vendored source with no lockfile
summary: An addon is a folder under res://addons/ with a plugin.cfg, enabled in Project Settings > Plugins; there is no dependency resolution, so commit the source and record the version and commit it came from.
detail: Godot 4.7 replaced the AssetLib browser with an Asset Store, which is a discovery surface, not a package manager. Two risks specific to this project: an addon that claims a class_name you also want, and an editor plugin that writes to project.godot on enable — read the diff the first time. For a one-owner project the correct addon count is close to zero: the tooling has to stay small, and every addon breaks on the next minor engine release and only you can fix it. Provenance goes in THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt the way the art already does.

name: which Godot version each annotation arrived in
summary: @static_unload is 4.1, @export_custom and @export_storage 4.3, @export_tool_button and @warning_ignore_start/_restore 4.4, @abstract 4.5.
detail: Established by diffing the @GDScript class reference across docs versions 4.1/4.2/4.3/4.4/4.5 against 4.7 stable. The full 4.7 annotation set is 36 entries; the rest (@export and its hint variants, @export_group/@export_subgroup/@export_category, @onready, @tool, @icon, @rpc, @warning_ignore) predate 4.1. @rpc is multiplayer-only and irrelevant to a single-player arcade.

name: Lock-free fan-out: element writes are thread-safe, resizes are not
summary: GDScript Array and Dictionary element reads and writes are safe across threads; anything that changes the container size is not — so size once, then let N workers write disjoint indices.
detail: This is the single most useful sentence on the Thread-safe APIs page and it removes the mutex from most parallel work: call resize() on the main thread before submitting, then have each add_group_task element write only its own index. append(), resize(), erase() and pop_* from a worker are the bug that reproduces once a week on one machine.

name: Autoloads: four, not forty
summary: Autoloads register under Project Settings > Globals > Autoload, become global identifiers added to root before any scene, and calling free()/queue_free() on one is a documented engine crash.
detail: A script autoload gets a bare Node created for it; a scene autoload is instantiated. List order is load order. The failure mode of over-using them is a project where every subsystem reaches every other and nothing can be exercised in isolation — exactly what Cosmo's typed host/scene boundary exists to prevent. For the rebuild: save store, music scheduler, run state, settings/telemetry. Everything else is a node in the scene it belongs to.

name: await, process_frame, and why await is not a thread
summary: await get_tree().process_frame resumes immediately before _process runs next frame; await hides latency on the main thread and never moves work off it.
detail: SceneTree.process_frame is 'emitted immediately before Node._process() is called on every node in this tree', and physics_frame is its physics counterpart — so a coroutine resuming on process_frame runs ahead of the frame's normal work and can be cut short by that frame's budget check. await replaces Godot 3's yield entirely. Do not await on a worker thread: resumption is driven by main-thread signal emission and the engine documents no thread contract for GDScript function state. Awaiting inside _ready() makes the node count as ready the moment the coroutine suspends. Awaiting something that is neither a signal nor a coroutine returns immediately with a runtime warning that static typing will not catch.

name: where await is a trap
summary: await resumes on the frame a signal fires, cannot be cancelled, makes every caller that wants a return value a coroutine, and returns instantly on anything that is not a signal.
detail: Unlike 3.x yield there is no function-state object, deliberately, so a coroutine waiting on a signal that never fires is parked forever holding its captures. Calling a coroutine without await is legal and runs asynchronously - enable MISSING_AWAIT, which defaults to IGNORE. The awaited value is the single argument, an Array for several, null for none. Fine for a one-shot delay; unusable as a scheduler.

name: Reproducing a build stamp without a bundler define
summary: Godot has no Vite-style define; generate game/build_stamp.gd from git in CI before exporting, or use an EditorExportPlugin._export_begin() with add_file().
detail: The generated-file route is deterministic and needs no editor plugin — keep a checked-in placeholder so the editor always parses. The EditorExportPlugin route stamps manual editor exports too, at the cost of a git subprocess inside the export path that fails on a machine without git on PATH. Either way the invariant is unchanged: a build stamp identifies source, never deployment. docs/invariants.md still governs.

name: call_deferred and set_deferred: the only safe way back to the scene tree
summary: Callable.call_deferred() queues a call that runs during idle time — mainly at the end of process and physics frames — and always returns null, not the method's result.
detail: Modern idiom is method.call_deferred(args) and node.set_deferred(&"property", value); the Godot 3 string form call_deferred("method", args) still works but is unchecked. Deferring a method from itself is infinite recursion, exactly as a direct call would be. Deferred is not 'next frame' — it may flush at the end of the current process frame — so use await get_tree().process_frame when a one-frame delay is what you meant. Ordering is queue order and is not ordered against signals emitted later in the frame.

name: Callables and lambda capture
summary: Lambdas capture locals by value once at creation, cannot reassign them, cannot be static or persistent, and two identically written lambdas are different disconnect targets.
detail: Callable == Callable is true only when both invoke the same custom target, so a lambda you did not store cannot be disconnected - the call is a silent no-op. bind() appends arguments after the emitted ones, unbind(n) drops the last n. Callable carries no signature in the type system: var f: Callable tells the analyzer nothing about arity or parameter types, so a dispatch table of Callables gets zero static checking.

name: --check-only parses one script, and script errors may not fail the process
summary: --check-only is documented as "Only parse for errors and quit (use with --script)" — one file at a time. Nothing documents a non-zero exit on a runtime script error.
detail: There is no documented flag that parses every script in a project and returns non-zero. Practical substitutes: run --headless --import once (parse errors surface on stderr), then loop --check-only over each .gd file. godot-proposals#13048 asks for structured headless error output precisely because errors today are unstructured and can drop the process into the interactive debugger, which is a CI hang. CI should grep stderr for SCRIPT ERROR / Parse Error / ERROR: in addition to checking the exit status. Sources: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/editor/command_line_tutorial.html and https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/13048

name: class_name, inner classes and @abstract
summary: class_name registers a global type, const preload keeps it file-local, inner classes keep row types beside their only user, and @abstract (4.5+) replaces the push_error base method.
detail: An abstract method has no body - a newline or semicolon follows the header - and any class with an unimplemented abstract method must itself be @abstract. Inner classes and class_name classes can both be abstract; an abstract script cannot be attached to a node. Preloaded scripts are conventionally PascalCase because they are types. Never write @export var x: PackedScene = preload(...): the stored scene value overwrites it and .new() ignores it.

name: Command-line export: import first, and paths are relative to the project
summary: --export-release <preset> <path> needs export templates installed and an export preset; output paths resolve against the project directory, not the working directory. --export-debug implies --import; --export-release does not say so.
detail: Documented at https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/export/exporting_projects.html and the command line tutorial. Run `godot --headless --path . --import` as its own step so the .godot cache exists and is cacheable; the community CI recipe adds `--headless --editor --quit` as a pre-heat when a cold cache makes the first export fail. Templates live at ~/.local/share/godot/export_templates/<version>.stable/ unpacked from the .tpz; 4.7 allows fetching a single platform's templates. --export-pack produces only the PCK/ZIP. Community reference: https://github.com/abarichello/godot-ci

name: const collections are read-only, but need constant expressions
summary: const arrays and dictionaries are automatically read-only in GDScript, but const requires a constant expression: preload() qualifies, Row.new() does not.
detail: So a literal table needs no make_read_only() and no defensive duplicate(). A table of typed row objects has three shapes: const arrays of literals (free read-only, no row type), a static var array of RefCounted rows built in _static_init() (typed fields, code-authored), or a container Resource with @export var rows: Array[RowType] and one .tres per row (inspector-editable and diffable). assert() is stripped from release builds, so a table-shape check must be an if plus push_error.

name: Authored tables become custom Resources; tuned scalars stay const
summary: Rings, worlds, orb pools, formation tiers and level windows want class_name X extends Resource with @export and typed Array[T]; a playtested number wants a const in a .gd, because .tres cannot hold its comment.
detail: Typed Array[OrbSpec] gives an inspector drag-target that rejects the wrong type; untyped Array does not. Resources are cached and SHARED — two scenes loading the same .tres get the same object, so treat specs as immutable or duplicate() explicitly. Never load() a resource from a player or server: a .tres names a script path and FileAccess.get_var(true) deserialises objects that can execute code. The const-vs-Resource split maps onto the database's own spec-vs-tuning distinction.

name: --fixed-fps and --disable-render-loop make a driven run reproducible
summary: --fixed-fps forces a fixed frame rate and "disables real-time synchronization"; --disable-render-loop renders only when script asks. Together they give a deterministic harness clock.
detail: Also useful: --quit-after <n> iterations, --time-scale, --max-fps, --print-fps. Verified at https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/editor/command_line_tutorial.html. Cosmo's harnesses already drive a fixed-step loop (drawcheck plays 2,400 frames); this is the flag set that reproduces that shape in Godot without a browser.

name: Godot 4.7 moved whole sections of the documentation
summary: contributing/development/... became engine_details/development/..., and the GDExtension pages moved under engine_details/engine_api/ — old links 404 rather than redirect.
detail: Written against 4.7.2-stable; docs.godotengine.org/en/stable serves the 4.7 branch. Pages that moved include Optimizing a build for size and Compiling with PCK encryption key (now under engine_details/development/compiling/) and the whole GDExtension section (now engine_details/engine_api/gdextension/). A 4.3 or 4.4 URL for any of these still resolves to the OLD version of the page, which is how stale claims get cited as current. Always check the version banner on a Godot docs page before quoting it.

name: EditorDock and add_dock() replaced add_control_to_dock() at 4.6
summary: 4.6+ uses EditorDock.new() with title/default_slot and EditorPlugin.add_dock()/remove_dock(); 4.5 and earlier use add_control_to_dock(DOCK_SLOT_*, control). EditorDock is marked experimental.
detail: Verified by comparing the Making Plugins page at /en/4.5/ (add_control_to_dock, remove_control_from_docks) with /en/stable/ and /en/4.6/ (EditorDock, add_dock, remove_dock, EditorDock.DOCK_LAYOUT_VERTICAL). The EditorDock class reference carries the experimental banner: "This class may be changed or removed in future versions." Pin the engine version if you ship a dock. Sources: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_editordock.html and https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/plugins/editor/making_plugins.html

name: EditorInspectorPlugin replaces a number field with a picture
summary: _can_handle(object) plus _parse_property(...) returning true removes the built-in editor; add_property_editor(name, control, add_to_end, label) inserts your own Control.
detail: Signatures verified at https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_editorinspectorplugin.html: _parse_property(object, type, name, hint_type, hint_string, usage_flags, wide) -> bool, plus _parse_begin/_parse_category/_parse_group/_parse_end and add_custom_control / add_property_editor_for_multiple_properties. Register with EditorPlugin.add_inspector_plugin() in _enter_tree() and remove it in _exit_tree(). Every script the editor loads — including the preview Control — needs @tool. Use EditorUndoRedoManager (get_undo_redo()) for any scene mutation.

name: EditorInterface is a global singleton since 4.2
summary: Any @tool script can call EditorInterface.get_resource_filesystem() directly; before 4.2 it was reachable only through an EditorPlugin or EditorScript instance.
detail: The 4.2 change removed the ad-hoc-instance hack that older tutorials still teach (creating an EditorScript just to reach the interface, or threading a plugin reference through every class). Source: godotengine/godot PR #75694, reflected in https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_editorinterface.html

name: Encrypted saves: two mechanisms, and why Cosmo wants neither
summary: FileAccess.open_encrypted_with_pass() needs no custom templates; PCK encryption needs SCRIPT_AES256_ENCRYPTION_KEY at engine compile time and 'will not work if you use official, precompiled export templates'.
detail: FileAccess.open_encrypted takes a 32-byte key; open_encrypted_with_pass derives one from a string; ConfigFile.save_encrypted_pass/load_encrypted_pass are the same idea one level up. The PCK route's own docs concede 'the key needs to be stored in the binary', so extraction is harder, not impossible. For Cosmo the whole game is already delivered to the browser and the repository is public; an encrypted local save adds a key you must never lose, breaks a player's ability to recover their own file, and buys nothing. The design already reached the right answer: server-side monotonic merge, which makes a forged best:0 a no-op.

name: RandomNumberGenerator's algorithm is not a stability promise
summary: Identical seeds reproduce a sequence, but Godot's docs say the underlying PCG32 implementation should not be relied on as a permanent detail — so golden tests seeded through it can silently change meaning.
detail: From https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_randomnumbergenerator.html. Practical rule for a rebuild: ship your own small PRNG in GDScript and inject it, exactly as tools/lib/rng.mjs injects a seeded Math into every Cosmo harness today. Prefer xorshift32 over a mulberry32 port: GDScript ints are 64-bit signed and a 32x32 multiply can overflow, so a shift/xor generator is the one that is obviously correct.

name: the @export hint vocabulary
summary: Beyond @export: or_greater/or_less, exp, hide_slider, suffix:, radians_as_degrees, groups and subgroups, typed resource arrays, @export_storage, @export_custom and @export_tool_button.
detail: Range hints ride @export_range as trailing strings. @export_group("") ends a group; groups cannot nest. Array[T] where T extends Resource accepts multi-file drag-and-drop. Packed arrays export only if initialised empty. @export_custom performs no validation on its hint string. @export_tool_button (4.4+) exports a Callable as an inspector button using engine icon names only - the cheapest content tool with no editor plugin.

name: Export presets, secrets and the CI command line
summary: Commit export_presets.cfg; never commit .godot/export_credentials.cfg. CI runs godot --headless --import first, then --export-release "<preset>" <path>.
detail: --headless is required on a runner with no GPU. --import 'starts the editor, waits for any resources to be imported, and then quits'; on a clean checkout with no .godot/ cache, skipping it ships a pack with unimported assets and no error you notice. Five resource export modes plus an include filter for non-resources (*.json, *.txt, *.csv) and an exclude filter — Godot's version of a publish allowlist, and weaker than Cosmo's, which fails the build rather than relying on a glob you remembered to write.

name: Custom export templates and what they actually cost
summary: Build profiles, disable_3d=yes (~15% for 2D), optimize=size or size_extra (4.5+), lto=full (12-16 GB RAM) and stripping (5-10x) shrink the binary — at the price of a toolchain per platform, forever.
detail: The build-profile route (scons build_profile=/path/to/profile.gdbuild) has the highest leverage: the editor detects which engine features the project touches. The docs warn detection 'may occasionally be too aggressive', so a custom-template build can run in the editor and crash on a stripped feature — verify by playing it. 4.7 added downloading only the platforms you need, which helps CI cache size. Optional ICU Data is a separate download and is what buys CJK/Thai and emoji.

name: @export_tool_button replaces the self-resetting bool hack (4.4+)
summary: @export_tool_button("Label") var action: Callable = _method exports a clickable inspector button. Requires a @tool class. Added in Godot 4.4.
detail: Documented at https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_exports.html: "If you need to create a clickable inspector button, you can use @export_tool_button. This exports a Callable property as a clickable button." A second argument names an editor icon from the engine's icon set; custom project icons are not supported. Before 4.4 the idiom was an exported bool that set itself back to false in its setter, which is the pattern to stop copying.

name: Feature-tag overrides, and the get_setting trap
summary: project.godot supports per-platform overrides with a suffix (renderer/rendering_method.web); ProjectSettings.get_setting() ignores them and returns the base value — only get_setting_with_override() respects them.
detail: This fails silently: the value returned is a value, just the wrong one, and the symptom is behaviour differing between editor and export for no visible reason. Default tags cover platforms (android/ios/web/windows/macos/linuxbsd), build types (debug/release/editor/template), architectures (arm64/wasm32/...), device classes (mobile/pc/web) and threads/nothreads. Custom feature tags are declared per export preset and do NOT apply when running from the editor, by design.

name: Slice amortised work by a microsecond deadline, never by item count
summary: Time.get_ticks_usec() plus await get_tree().process_frame gives a budget that degrades gracefully on slow devices; a fixed N-per-frame is a budget in the wrong unit.
detail: Arm a deadline of Time.get_ticks_usec() + budget, do one unit, check, and await process_frame when spent. The check happens after a unit, so the unit must fit inside the budget — a 12ms unit blows a 2ms budget however the loop is written; the fix is to split the unit, not lower the budget. Deadlines compose (two jobs can share one budget object and the total stays bounded) and counts do not. Do this in _process, not _physics_process, because physics can run several times per rendered frame when catching up and silently multiplies the budget.

name: GDExtension: the real cost and the five signs that justify it
summary: One compiled artifact per platform and architecture, forced cross-origin isolation on web, godot-cpp pinned to an engine API version, and native stacks instead of GDScript ones.
detail: Justified only when: the profiler shows SCRIPT time dominating a frame missing 16.6 ms on the target device; the hot path is a tight numeric loop over thousands of elements that is not expressible as a shader, MultiMesh or a servers call; per-frame allocation is already gone; everything is already statically typed; or you need a native library with no GDScript equivalent. Cosmo hits none — the heaviest work is shader work on the GPU, the simulation is dozens of entities, and the scheduler's difficulty is timing, not throughput. Reach for RenderingServer and MultiMeshInstance2D first.

name: .gdignore hides a directory from the whole engine
summary: An empty .gdignore file stops Godot importing or parsing a directory and hides it from the FileSystem dock — but load() and preload() can no longer reach anything inside it.
detail: Quote: "Once the folder is ignored, resources in that folder can't be loaded anymore using the load() and preload() methods." Use it for raw art sources kept beside exported PNGs and for scratch/research directories. Do NOT put a tools/ directory behind it — harness scripts must stay loadable by --script. Source: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/best_practices/project_organization.html

name: GDScript's honest performance ceiling
summary: GDScript is a bytecode VM with no JIT - the manual lists JIT/AOT as planned - and every property or method access walks the script and then ClassDB.
detail: This is the one place the rebuild is plainly worse off than the current stack: Cosmo's 12k-line runtime is executed by a JIT-compiling JavaScript engine today. Mitigations that are documented rather than folklore: type everything so the VM picks specialised opcodes, prefer typed global math functions, keep per-frame entities as flat RefCounted rows rather than nodes, and move genuinely hot bulk work to packed arrays or to the servers. Any specific speed claim beyond these should be measured in the project's own build.

name: gdtoolkit is the only part of the toolchain that runs without the engine
summary: pip install "gdtoolkit==4.*" gives gdformat and gdlint, which parse GDScript standalone — a fast CI pre-pass, but blind to the engine's type system.
detail: gdformat --check src/ fails on unformatted files; gdlint src/ finds style and shape smells. It does not know class hierarchies or property types, so it finds none of what the unsafe_* warnings find. Run both; they do not overlap. Current PyPI release 4.3.2 as read 2026-09-07. Source: https://github.com/Scony/godot-gdscript-toolkit

name: gdUnit4 vs GUT: what each can and cannot test
summary: gdUnit4 (v6.2.1, Godot 4.5-4.7.1) has a touch-capable scene runner, C# support and a maintained GitHub Action; GUT (9.7.1) has better doubles and less machinery. Neither runs without the engine.
detail: gdUnit4: extends GdUnitTestSuite, fluent assert_str(x).is_equal(y), CLI addons/gdUnit4/runtest.sh, exit codes 0 pass / 100 failures / 101 warnings, JUnit XML + HTML, refuses headless without --ignoreHeadlessMode. GUT: extends GutTest, assert_eq(a, b, msg), CLI godot -d -s --path "$PWD" addons/gut/gut_cmdln.gd with -gdir/-gtest/-gexit/-gjunit_xml_file, exit 0 pass / 1 any failure. Both lag engine releases, which is a recurring upgrade tax Cosmo does not pay today with harnesses it owns outright. Sources: https://github.com/godot-gdunit-labs/gdUnit4 and https://github.com/bitwes/Gut

name: Godot 3 idiom that fills search results and is wrong in 4.7
summary: yield->await, export var->@export, setget->property setters, the Tween node->create_tween(), the old connect signature->signal.connect(), File/Directory->FileAccess/DirAccess, JavaScript->JavaScriptBridge.
detail: Also: KinematicBody2D->CharacterBody2D, OS.get_screen_size and friends->DisplayServer.*, the tool keyword->@tool. Godot 4-specific traps on the same ground: get_setting() ignoring feature overrides; uncommitted *.uid; committed .godot/ leaking keystore passwords; skipping --import in CI; assuming file:// works; assuming AudioEffects work on web; assuming PCK encryption works with official templates; renaming the project and orphaning every save; free()ing an autoload; and 4.7's moved doc URLs 404ing rather than redirecting.

name: Godot 3 idiom that must never appear
summary: yield, setget, export(Type), connect with string method names, Tween nodes, instance(), Pool*Array and Reference are all 3.x; each has a different 4.x spelling.
detail: yield(obj,"sig") is await obj.sig; var x setget set_x,get_x is an inline set:/get: block or var x: set = set_x, get = get_x; export(int) var x is @export var x: int; obj.connect("sig", self, "_on") is obj.sig.connect(_on); Tween as a node is create_tween(); KinematicBody2D/move_and_slide(vel, UP) is CharacterBody2D with velocity then move_and_slide(); PackedScene.instance() is instantiate(); PoolFloatArray is PackedFloat32Array; OS.get_ticks_msec is Time.get_ticks_msec; Reference is RefCounted; an abstract base that push_errors is @abstract (4.5+).

name: Capturing a frame for pixel regression tests
summary: await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw, then get_viewport().get_texture().get_image() and Image.save_png(). Requires a display server — it returns nothing useful under --headless.
detail: Compare statistically, not exactly: Cosmo's rendercheck already grades edge discontinuity, glow energy ratio, per-world mean/p10/p90 and hue-vs-composition distinctness rather than pixel equality, and that is the right choice across drivers and software rasterizers. Godot has no official screenshot-testing framework; community addons exist (GDSnap) but should be treated as leads. For a frame-exact sequence, Movie Maker mode is the deterministic capture path.

name: Input events do not propagate under --headless
summary: Input.parse_input_event() is dropped in headless mode (godot#73557, open since 4.0 RC2), which is why gdUnit4's CLI refuses headless unless you pass --ignoreHeadlessMode.
detail: gdUnit4's command-line documentation states headless is disabled by default "to prevent test errors that inevitably occur during UI tests, since Godot cannot process UI input in headless mode". Consequence for a rebuild: any test that drives real taps or swipes needs either a display server or a seam below Input that gameplay consumes instead of the engine's input singleton. Sources: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/73557 and https://godot-gdunit-labs.github.io/gdUnit4/latest/advanced_testing/cmd/

name: --headless disables all rendering, so no pixel check can run in it
summary: Godot's --headless is --display-driver headless --audio-driver Dummy; DisplayServer docs state it disables all rendering and window management. Screenshots need a real display server.
detail: Quote: "Starting the engine with the --headless command line argument disables all rendering and window management functions. Most functions from DisplayServer will return dummy values in this case." Offscreen/surfaceless rendering is still only a proposal (godot-proposals#5790) at 4.7.2. A CI pixel lane therefore needs Xvfb plus a software rasterizer (Godot's own godot-benchmarks runs its GPU suite under a headless X11 display) or a GPU runner. Sources: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_displayserver.html and https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/editor/command_line_tutorial.html

name: Bake Image on a worker, upload ImageTexture on the main thread
summary: Image is CPU-side and safe to build off-thread; ImageTexture is a GPU object whose creation off-thread stalls the RenderingServer — and Image.create() is deprecated in favour of create_empty().
detail: Image.create_empty(width, height, use_mipmaps, format) is the current static constructor; Image.create() is marked deprecated in the 4.7 reference and create_empty does not exist in the 4.2 reference, so it is 4.3+. ImageTexture.create_from_image(image) allocates; set_image() reallocates; update(image) reuses the allocation and requires matching size, format and mipmap configuration, and is documented as faster for frequent updates. Split any procedural sprite bake along that line: pixels in parallel, upload serial.

name: member initialization order
summary: Defaults, then declarations top to bottom, then _init(), then exported values, then @onready, then _ready(); reading an export inside _init() gives the annotation default.
detail: Two consequences bite: @onready and @export on one variable is broken by construction because @onready runs after the export is applied and overwrites it (ONREADY_WITH_EXPORT is an error-level warning by default), and a declaration whose initializer calls a helper touching a member declared below it gets clobbered by that member's own initializer. A Resource has no _ready, so read exported values in the property's setter.

name: JavaScriptBridge is registered on every platform, stubbed off-web
summary: platform/web/api/api.cpp guards its bodies with #if !defined(WEB_ENABLED) and platform/SCsub compiles every platform's api/*.cpp into every build, so JavaScriptBridge.eval() compiles everywhere and returns null off-web.
detail: That makes a same-origin localStorage read safe to write once and guard with OS.has_feature("web"), with no conditional compilation and no Engine.get_singleton() dance. eval(code, use_global_execution_context) runs in the page's window, so any key the previous build wrote to that origin is readable. Verified by reading the 4.7 source, not inferred from the class reference, which only says the singleton is web-only.

name: Localisation structure, and the decision to make now
summary: CSV imports to .translation, registered under Project Settings > Localization > Translations, read with tr() and tr_n(), with a Remaps tab that swaps whole resources per locale.
detail: The structural decision is not the pipeline, it is not scattering literal strings through the code: writing tr(&"LESSON_FIRST_HOP") costs nothing today and makes the teaching copy addressable. Cosmo has 103 lesson records; retrofitting keys onto them later is the expensive version. The real cost of ever shipping a locale is glyph coverage — the optional ICU Data export-template download is what buys CJK and Thai. Budget the font, not the CSV.

name: match strictness and enum typing
summary: match is stricter than == (1 does not match 1.0; String does match StringName) and supports when guards; a named enum is a constant Dictionary whose type is just int.
detail: Patterns are literal, constant expression or A.B attribute access, wildcard _, binding var name, array and dictionary patterns with .. for open ends, comma-separated alternatives, and when guards evaluated only after the pattern matches. 3.x's special continue inside match was removed in 4.0. An enum type guarantees nothing about the value belonging to the set, so keep INT_AS_ENUM_WITHOUT_CAST and ENUM_VARIABLE_WITHOUT_DEFAULT on.

name: Measure the worst frame, not the average framerate
summary: Engine.get_frames_per_second() is an average and hides the single 40ms frame the player actually feels; use Time.get_ticks_usec() deltas and record the maximum.
detail: get_frames_per_second() is documented as 'the average frames rendered every second'. Time.get_ticks_usec() is monotonic microseconds since engine start on a 64-bit value. Engine.get_process_frames() increments every process frame 'regardless of whether the render loop is enabled', which makes it a reliable once-per-frame guard. A hitch is a distribution tail, so instrument for the tail.

name: The deferred-call queue is finite and drops calls silently
summary: memory/limits/message_queue/max_size_mb defaults to 32MB; overflow prints "Message queue out of memory" and discards the call rather than crashing.
detail: core/object/message_queue.cpp prints 'Failed method: %s. Message queue out of memory.' and equivalents for deferred sets and notifications. The failure mode is a silently skipped update, which is far harder to diagnose than a crash. Anything that defers once per object per frame across hundreds of objects will reach it: defer one batch, not N items.

name: Movie Maker mode is Godot's deterministic capture
summary: --write-movie runs the engine non-real-time at a fixed FPS: "faster hardware will allow you to render a given animation in less time, but the visual output remains identical".
detail: Combine with --fixed-fps to pin the rate. This is the right tool for a golden sequence rather than a single frame — an earned drop, a starfall release, a world morph — where one frame cannot show whether the envelope landed on the beat. Output is AVI or a PNG sequence. Source: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/animation/creating_movies.html

name: Native lifecycle and haptics without a WebView bridge
summary: NOTIFICATION_APPLICATION_PAUSED/RESUMED (Android and iOS), FOCUS_IN/FOCUS_OUT, WM_GO_BACK_REQUEST and set_auto_accept_quit(false) replace the whole Capacitor bridge; Input.vibrate_handheld is far blunter than @capacitor/haptics.
detail: MainLoop defines APPLICATION_RESUMED=2014, APPLICATION_PAUSED=2015, APPLICATION_FOCUS_IN=2016, APPLICATION_FOCUS_OUT=2017 and OS_MEMORY_WARNING=2009 (iOS). WM_GO_BACK_REQUEST fires on Android Back while Application > Config > Quit On Go Back is enabled, which is the default. Input.vibrate_handheld(duration_ms:int=500, amplitude:float=-1.0) is one blunt pulse — Cosmo's six haptic kinds, its 65 ms rate limit and its priority ordering all have to be rebuilt in GDScript over that primitive.

name: AudioServer and RenderingServer cannot be stubbed from GDScript
summary: Godot's engine singletons are C++ with no injection point, and neither gdUnit4 nor GUT can double them — so recorded-call harnesses have no direct equivalent.
detail: This is the structural reason Cosmo's three strongest harnesses do not port. musiccheck.mjs stubs AudioContext in a vm and records every oscillator start, frequency and gain write; fxcheck.mjs hands the runtime a fake WebGL context that parses uniform declarations out of the shader; drawcheck.mjs records every 2D call. None of those substitutions is expressible in Godot. The only recovery is architectural: make the decision a pure function that returns typed data, and keep the engine call a thin dumb consumer.

name: Performance monitors and viewport render timing, with their limits
summary: Performance.get_monitor() covers frame time, draw calls, orphan nodes and memory; RenderingServer.viewport_get_measured_render_time_gpu() gives GPU ms — but returns 0.0 on Metal and needs rendering.
detail: Enable per-viewport timing with RenderingServer.viewport_set_measure_render_time(rid, true). Several monitors refresh at most once per second ("there may be a delay of up to 1 second between changes"), so sample over seconds. OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT is the cheapest real regression check and it works headless — it catches leaked nodes on teardown. Godot's own godot-benchmarks is the reference pattern: run a scene five seconds, log average per-frame statistics, emit JSON, diff against a baseline. CI on a software rasterizer proves counts, not frame rate; frame rate is a device measurement. Sources: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_performance.html and https://github.com/godotengine/godot-benchmarks

name: Shader pipeline compilation is a frame-time cliff your own code cannot fix
summary: The first draw of a material variant compiles a GPU pipeline; ubershaders are 4.4+, the Shader Baker export option is 4.5+ and is not supported on web.
detail: Ubershaders (4.4+) precompile one general pipeline using specialization constants and compile optimised variants in the background during play. The Shader Baker export option (4.5+) bundles compiled shader code into the PCK so the compilation step is skipped entirely — Forward+ and Mobile renderers only, not Compatibility, on Windows (Vulkan/D3D12), macOS (Vulkan/Metal), Linux (Vulkan) and Android (Vulkan), and not on web. The universal fallback is still to render every material once, invisible or off-camera, during loading.

name: Portrait mobile project settings
summary: stretch/mode canvas_items with stretch/aspect expand and handheld/orientation portrait; the docs' mobile example is 720x1280 with 1080x1920 offered for high-end devices.
detail: canvas_items renders at device resolution and scales the 2D coordinate system, keeping text and shader output crisp; viewport renders at the base size and blits, avoiding scaling artifacts but discarding resolution. expand grows the viewport in the long axis rather than letterboxing, which is what makes a 19.5:9 phone usable — and which means the visible height is NOT fixed. Any rebuild that hard-codes 1920 will look wrong on a 20:9 phone. Cosmo already lives under this constraint in Phaser.

name: Godot 4 project layout and naming
summary: snake_case for every file and folder, PascalCase for node names and class_name; group by subsystem or content type but never both; .gdignore is an empty file, not a pattern file.
detail: snake_case is not taste: Windows and macOS are case-insensitive while Linux and the exporter are not, so res://Art/Comet.png can resolve locally and fail on a Linux CI export. GDScript has no namespaces, so class_name is a project-wide claim that collides with addons — prefix generic names. An empty .gdignore makes the importer skip a directory and hides it from the FileSystem dock; its contents are ignored.

name: property setters and getters in 4.x
summary: set/get accessors always run, including from inside the class, but never during initialization; inline accessors cannot carry type hints and the variable's own name bypasses them.
detail: This is the opposite of 3.x setget, which did not fire on internal access. Using the property's own name inside its accessor reads or writes the underlying member, which is what prevents infinite recursion - but only for the inline form; a separated setter assigning through the property name does recurse. The initializer writes straight through the setter even with @export or @onready applied. Inline and separated notations cannot be mixed on one variable.

name: RefCounted vs Object vs Node
summary: RefCounted frees itself and is the documented default for custom data; nodes add tree membership, notifications and scripting-API cost that flat entity rows never use.
detail: Godot reference-counts rather than collecting garbage: RefCounted and Resource free when the last reference drops, Object and Node live until free()/queue_free(). Cycles never free - weakref() breaks them, is_instance_valid() tests a raw Object. The data-preferences page explains why the scripting API is slow: every property or method access walks the script then the inheritance chain through ClassDB. That is the argument for typed fields on RefCounted rows over nodes with exported properties.

name: ConfigFile or JSON for saves, never store_var
summary: ConfigFile gives load/save/parse plus encrypted variants; its documented trap is that section and property names cannot contain spaces — anything after a space is dropped on save and on load.
detail: FileAccess.store_var/get_var is not a save format: get_var(allow_objects=true) deserialises objects that 'can contain code which gets executed'. Godot does not write atomically either — an interrupted cfg.save(PATH) leaves a truncated file — so write to PATH + '.tmp' and rename through DirAccess. That pattern should hold on web too, since the rename goes through the same virtual filesystem, but the IndexedDB-backed FS is the least-exercised path here and is worth verifying rather than assuming.

name: A SceneTree script is Godot's headless harness entry point
summary: godot --headless -s res://tools/x.gd runs a script that must extend SceneTree or MainLoop; SceneTree.quit(exit_code) is what makes CI red.
detail: Documented at https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/editor/command_line_tutorial.html ("-s, --script <script>") and https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_scenetree.html ("void quit(exit_code: int = 0)" — "Quits the application at the end of the current iteration, with the given exit_code"). MainLoop's _process(delta) returns true to end the loop. This replaces Cosmo's vm-sandbox harnesses entirely: no source extraction, no marker pair, no line-number padding — a harness just preloads the class it tests.

name: Shader.get_shader_uniform_list() is the fxcheck uniform-name equivalent
summary: Loading a Shader and reading its uniform list lets a test assert that every parameter name the game sets actually exists — the typo class that both WebGL and Godot ignore silently.
detail: Signature: Array get_shader_uniform_list(get_groups: bool = false), "Returns the list of shader uniforms that can be assigned to a ShaderMaterial". ShaderMaterial.set_shader_parameter's docs stress the name "is case-sensitive and must match the name of the uniform in the code exactly", and say nothing about erroring on an unknown name. UNVERIFIED: whether the list is populated under --headless, since the dummy rasterizer may not parse the shader — test it, and if it comes back empty run the check in the display lane or fall back to parsing the .gdshader text. Source: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_shader.html

name: the 4.x signal idiom
summary: Signals are first-class objects: sig.connect(callable) and sig.emit(args), never connect("sig", self, "_on_sig"); connect returns an error code and takes ConnectFlags.
detail: Flags: CONNECT_DEFERRED (runs at idle, end of frame), CONNECT_PERSIST (serialised with the scene, unusable with lambdas), CONNECT_ONE_SHOT, CONNECT_REFERENCE_COUNTED, CONNECT_APPEND_SOURCE_OBJECT. Connecting the same Callable twice returns ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER and prints an error unless reference-counted. If a connected callable's object is freed the connection is dropped for you - convenient, and a silent behaviour change.

name: Godot 4.7.2 is the stable release this handbook targets
summary: Godot 4.7.2-stable shipped 2026-08-18; docs.godotengine.org/en/stable is the 4.7 documentation, and 4.8 is in dev. Version-gate every API claim against it.
detail: Verified from https://godotengine.org/download/archive/ and https://godotengine.org/releases/4.7/ on 2026-09-07. 4.7 itself landed 2026-06-18, 4.7.1 on 2026-07-14. This matters because Godot 3 idiom dominates search results and several 4.x APIs moved inside the 4.x line (EditorInterface singleton at 4.2, @export_tool_button and .uid files at 4.4, EditorDock at 4.6).

name: static var, static func and _static_init
summary: static var (4.1), static func and the _static_init() static constructor give a typed table namespace with no node and no autoload; @static_unload is documented as not actually freeing.
detail: _static_init() runs when the class loads, after static variables initialise, takes no arguments and returns nothing. @export and @onready cannot apply to a static variable and locals cannot be static. Static variables keep the script resource loaded; the manual carries a standing warning that 'due to a bug, scripts are never freed, even if @static_unload annotation is used', so treat static state as permanent and small.

name: what static typing actually buys
summary: Typed GDScript buys correctness, editor completion, and 'optimized opcodes when operand/argument types are known at compile time' - and nothing more; there is no JIT.
detail: The manual's only performance claim is the optimized-opcodes sentence, on the same page that lists JIT/AOT as a planned future feature. So typed code is faster than untyped code by instruction selection, not by compilation. Size of the win depends on how much of a hot loop is arithmetic the analyzer can specialise; treat any number you read online as unverified.

name: StringName and the & prefix
summary: &"name" interns a string so comparison is identity rather than content; use it for keys, input actions, method and signal names, and note match treats "x" and &"x" as equal.
detail: StringNames are unique instances: two with the same value are the same object, which makes comparison 'extremely fast compared to regular Strings' while construction is the expensive part. Strings passed to StringName parameters convert automatically, 'often at compile time' - but a runtime-built String converts on every call. Not for player-facing text or anything sliced or formatted.

name: Thread, Mutex and Semaphore, and when they beat the pool
summary: A long-lived worker that owns a queue and sleeps on a Semaphore is the one case where Thread beats WorkerThreadPool; the join in _exit_tree is mandatory and Godot's Mutex is reentrant.
detail: A pool task that never returns permanently occupies a worker, so a persistent worker must be a real Thread. There is no cancel: cooperate with a flag under a mutex, post the semaphore to wake it, then wait_to_finish(). A Thread reaching refcount zero while started, holding a mutex, or waiting on a semaphore is a crash. Mutex is reentrant — lock twice, unlock twice — and try_lock() returns true if the caller already owns it, which hides double-lock bugs. Semaphore.post(count=1) can release several waiters; try_wait() is the non-blocking form. The manual warns that creating threads is slow, especially on Windows, and that mutex lock/unlock is itself expensive.

name: What is and is not thread-safe in Godot 4
summary: The scene tree is not thread-safe for reads or writes; most servers are; resources may be loaded on threads but not mutated from two; AStar is not.
detail: From the Thread-safe APIs manual page for 4.7: interacting with the active scene tree is not thread-safe — use call_deferred/set_deferred. Building a scene chunk outside the tree on a thread and then add_child.call_deferred() is the sanctioned pattern. Instancing nodes that render is unsafe unless Rendering > Threads > Thread Model is Multi-Threaded, which the same page says has several known bugs. Avoid GPU work off-thread (texture creation, image readback) because it stalls against the RenderingServer. RenderingServer.call_on_render_thread(callable) is the supported way to reach rendering internals.

name: ResourceLoader threaded loading, and the ways it still blocks
summary: load_threaded_request / load_threaded_get_status / load_threaded_get; get() blocks if the load is unfinished, and status must be polled at most once per process frame.
detail: Signatures: load_threaded_request(path, type_hint="", use_sub_threads=false, cache_mode=CACHE_MODE_REUSE) -> Error; load_threaded_get_status(path, progress: Array = []) -> ThreadLoadStatus; load_threaded_get(path) -> Resource. Status is INVALID_RESOURCE 0, IN_PROGRESS 1, FAILED 2, LOADED 3. CacheMode IGNORE 0, REUSE 1, REPLACE 2, IGNORE_DEEP 3, REPLACE_DEEP 4 — the DEEP variants are 4.3+. use_sub_threads recursively parallelises dependencies and the class reference warns it can cause in-game slowdowns because one load can saturate the shared pool. Loads are submitted to WorkerThreadPool via add_native_task, so they compete with your own tasks. resource_loader.cpp detects the main thread polling the same task twice within one Engine.get_process_frames() value and forces progress ('Support userland polling in a loop on the main thread'), so a busy-wait terminates — while freezing the frame. Prefer change_scene_to_packed() over change_scene_to_file(), which loads synchronously.

name: @tool is contagious and lies about static variables
summary: Any script a @tool script instantiates must also be @tool, subclasses do not inherit tool mode, and a non-tool script reading a static variable gets null with no warning.
detail: Static methods, constants and enums are reachable from a tool script without @tool on the target; static variables are the documented exception and silently read null. Editor-time edits have no undo, and queue_free()/free() inside a tool script can crash the editor. Guard side effects with Engine.is_editor_hint().

name: @tool scripts run in the editor with no undo and no watchdog
summary: Editor-time modifications are permanent, queue_free() during editor logic can crash, an infinite loop freezes the editor, and a plugin script without @tool "acts like an empty file".
detail: All four are stated in Godot's own documentation. The discipline that follows: a @tool script may compute and draw (_draw() writes nothing) but must not start clocks, touch user://, spawn, or free nodes — guard those paths with `if Engine.is_editor_hint(): return`. Enable the MISSING_TOOL warning as an error; it fires on the exact shape of the "acts like an empty file" bug. EditorScript (@tool extends EditorScript, _run()) is the one-shot escape hatch, run from Script editor File > Run. Sources: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/plugins/running_code_in_the_editor.html and https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/plugins/editor/making_plugins.html

name: What a .tscn diff can and cannot tell a reviewer
summary: Scenes are line-oriented text with a uid header, ext_resource/sub_resource entries and per-node ids — greppable, but a node reorder produces a diff nobody can review as intent.
detail: Header: [gd_scene format=3 uid="uid://..."] (load_steps deprecated at 4.6). References: [ext_resource type="Texture2D" uid="uid://..." path="res://..." id="2_eorut"]. Community folklore says Godot regenerates every resource id on save; there WAS a 4.1 regression doing exactly that (godot#77172) and whether any churn remains at 4.7 is unverified. Read git diff before committing a scene. Merge drivers exist (gdmerge, tscnmerge) but matter little for a single maintainer pushing to main. The practical conclusion is the opposite one: keep content in typed Resource files and code so the review surface stays in .gd and .tres. Source: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/engine_details/file_formats/tscn.html

name: typed arrays and typed dictionaries
summary: Array[T] since 4.0, Dictionary[K,V] since 4.4, nested typed collections never; the element type applies to [], assignment and for, but not to methods.
detail: So typed_array.pop_back() and dict.get(k, d) return Variant, which with INFERENCE_ON_VARIANT at its ERROR default will not compile behind :=. Assigning an untyped Array into a typed one fails; Array.assign() resizes and converts. duplicate() is shallow, duplicate_deep() arrived in 4.5. Typed for-loop variables (for x: T in xs) arrived in 4.2.

name: typed replacements for the global math functions
summary: abs/clamp/lerp/round/sign/snapped/floor/ceil/min/max take and return Variant; absf, clampf, lerpf, roundi, signf, snappedf, floori, minf and maxf are the typed counterparts.
detail: The static typing page lists these as 'common unsafe operations and their safe counterparts' and instructs using the typed forms whenever possible - they are what keeps an arithmetic-heavy loop on safe lines and typed opcodes. All names verified present in doc/classes/@GlobalScope.xml at 4.7-stable. Watch INTEGER_DIVISION when porting expressions like min(1, dl/150).

name: typed signal parameters are advisory
summary: Signal parameter types are documentation only: neither arity nor type is checked at emit, and the tracker issue asking for it was closed as not planned.
detail: The manual says the declared arguments show in the editor's Signals dock and generate callbacks, but 'you can still emit any number of arguments when you emit signals; it's up to you to emit the correct values'. Godot issue #110573, filed against 4.4.1/4.5 for exactly this, is closed as not planned. Consequence for a rebuild: signal contracts are held by harnesses, not by the compiler.

name: UID sidecar files (4.4+) must be committed and must travel with the file
summary: Godot 4.4 generalized uid:// identifiers to scripts, shaders and scenes with .uid sidecars. Gitignoring them makes every clone mint fresh UIDs and breaks scene-to-script references.
detail: They are project state, not build output, and the same rule as .import applies. Moving a script outside the editor means moving its .uid too; the editor then resolves the UID and rewrites referencing scenes on save. For a single-maintainer repository this is low-drama, but it is silent and delayed when it goes wrong. Source: https://godotengine.org/article/uid-changes-coming-to-godot-4-4/

name: *.uid files must be committed; .godot/ must not
summary: Since Godot 4.4 every resource, script and shader gets a .uid sidecar and references are stored as uid://; not committing them works locally and breaks on a fresh clone.
detail: The official 4.4 announcement is explicit that *.uid should NOT be gitignored. Without them references fall back to path resolution with warnings, and two resources swapping positions is undetectable. Move or delete the .uid alongside any script moved outside the editor. Gitignore .godot/ (which contains export_credentials.cfg, so ignoring the folder covers the secret) and *.translation. Use Project > Version Control > Generate Version Control Metadata — the 3.x/4.0 ignore lists circulating online are wrong for 4.1+ and will commit secrets.

name: `as` fails to null, silently
summary: Casting an object with `as` yields null on a type mismatch with no error, so the editor's green 'safe line' can be less reliable than the untyped form that errors at load.
detail: The manual's own example: `@onready var a := $N as T` is a safe line that silently becomes null if the scene changes, while `@onready var b: T = $N` is flagged unsafe but fails loudly at scene load. Reserve `as` for cases where null is a meaningful answer you immediately test. To reach into a Variant safely the documented pattern is Object.get() then an `is` check then a typed local.

name: user:// across platforms, and why the project name is load-bearing
summary: user:// is %APPDATA%/Godot/app_userdata/<project> on Windows, ~/Library/Application Support/... on macOS, ~/.local/share/godot/... on Linux, app-private on mobile, and an IndexedDB virtual filesystem on web.
detail: res:// is not writable in an exported project; only user:// is documented as guaranteed writable. The path derives from the project NAME, so renaming the project orphans every save — set application/config/use_custom_user_dir and a stable custom_user_dir_name on day one. This is the exact analogue of Cosmo's existing rule that the Capacitor scheme must not change because localStorage is origin-scoped. On web, FileAccess writes sync to IndexedDB automatically; force_fs_sync() exists only for modules that cannot use FileAccess. IndexedDB is site data, so a cleared browser or a private window has no save.

name: What a Godot 4 repository commits and what it ignores
summary: Ignore .godot/, *.translation, export_credentials.cfg. Commit every *.import file, every *.uid file and export_presets.cfg. Secrets live in .godot/export_credentials.cfg, not in the preset.
detail: The import documentation is explicit: "Make sure to commit these files to your version control system, as these files contain important metadata." The export documentation says export_presets.cfg "can be safely committed to version control" while .godot/export_credentials.cfg holds "passwords and encryption keys" and "should generally not be committed". The canonical ignore file is github/gitignore's Godot.gitignore (.godot/, .nomedia, .import/, export.cfg, export_credentials.cfg, *.tmp, *.translation). In CI, cache .godot/imported specifically — not all of .godot/. Sources: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/assets_pipeline/import_process.html and https://github.com/github/gitignore/blob/main/Godot.gitignore

name: Godot 4.7.2 language baseline
summary: The rebuild's language baseline: Godot 4.7.2 is current stable (18 Aug 2026), docs.godotengine.org/en/stable is 4.7, and every 4.x feature below it is available.
detail: 4.7 stable released 18 June 2026; 4.7.1 in July, 4.7.2 in August 2026; 4.8 is in dev snapshots. Verified from the official download page and the engine blog. Anything a session reads that says 'Godot 4' without a minor version must be checked against the gates in research.godot.annotation-availability and research.godot.typed-collections.

name: GDScript warning defaults ship permissive
summary: UNTYPED_DECLARATION and every UNSAFE_* warning default to IGNORE in gdscript_warning.h; a typed codebase has to raise them to Error in project settings itself.
detail: Read from modules/gdscript/gdscript_warning.h at the 4.7-stable tag. Four warnings default to ERROR (INFERENCE_ON_VARIANT, NATIVE_METHOD_OVERRIDE, GET_NODE_DEFAULT_WITHOUT_ONREADY, ONREADY_WITH_EXPORT). Settings live at debug/gdscript/warnings/<lowercase_name> under Project Settings > Debug > GDScript with Advanced Settings on. @warning_ignore(name), and @warning_ignore_start/_restore (4.4+), suppress locally.

name: GDScript warnings as errors are the cheapest harness in the project
summary: debug/gdscript/warnings/<name> takes 0=Ignore, 1=Warn, 2=Error. Setting untyped_declaration and the four unsafe_* warnings to 2 turns a class of runtime bugs into compile errors.
detail: WarnLevel { IGNORE, WARN, ERROR } is verified in modules/gdscript/gdscript_warning.h at the 4.7-stable tag; the 46 live warning codes are in the same file, and the project-setting key is the enum name lowercased (untyped_declaration, inferred_declaration, unsafe_property_access, unsafe_method_access, unsafe_cast, unsafe_call_argument, unsafe_void_return, native_method_override, missing_tool, narrowing_conversion, integer_division ...). Several typing warnings ship as IGNORE because "static typing is optional". Set debug/gdscript/warnings/exclude_addons=true or third-party addons turn CI red. @warning_ignore_start()/@warning_ignore_restore() (4.4+) suppress a region. Source: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/warning_system.html

name: Web audio: Sample mode has no AudioEffects, Stream mode has latency
summary: Web exports default to Sample playback, where AudioEffects are not supported; Stream playback restores them but 'incurs increased latency if threads are not enabled', and threads need cross-origin isolation.
detail: AudioServer.PLAYBACK_TYPE_SAMPLE is documented as 'Only currently supported on the web platform. AudioEffects are not supported when playback is considered as a sample.' The default is set by audio/general/default_playback_type and its .web override, and per node by AudioStreamPlayer.playback_type — which is itself marked experimental and 'may be changed or removed in future versions'. This is the single hardest constraint the web export puts on Cosmo, whose music is a scheduled synthesis chain with a bus and a measured make-up gain.

name: The web export's initial download, measured against Cosmo's
summary: Godot 4.3's engine .wasm was ~40 MB uncompressed and ~5 MB Brotli; Cosmo's entire current first load is 439,055 B of gzipped JS plus 788,521 B of WebP. Assume a 5-10x regression.
detail: The 4.3 figures are the only official ones published; 4.7's are not, and were not measured here — treat ~5 MB Brotli as an order of magnitude, not a promise. Measured in this checkout on 2026-09-07: dist/ is 4,004,830 B across 47 files, dist/assets/index-DG2O-aGv.js is 1,621,182 B (439,055 B gzipped), public/art/ is 788,521 B across 25 files. Serve .wasm as application/wasm and precompress; GitHub Pages gzips automatically, itch.io does not, GitLab Pages needs manual precompression, Netlify does Brotli — so the Pages copy will be heavier than the Netlify one.

name: What the Godot web export requires
summary: WebAssembly and WebGL 2.0 via the Compatibility renderer only; single-threaded is the default since 4.3, and Thread Support or Extensions Support both require COOP same-origin and COEP require-corp headers.
detail: Those two headers gate SharedArrayBuffer and, once set, stop the page freely embedding or calling other origins — the thing that broke Godot games on itch.io. Progressive Web App > Enable installs a service-worker workaround that simulates the headers when you cannot set them on the host. Forward+ and Mobile renderers do not export to web at all. The export cannot be opened over file://; it needs a server, the same constraint CLAUDE.md already states for the Vite entry.

name: What an iPhone player actually gets from the web export
summary: Godot's docs recommend Chromium or Firefox because 'Safari has several issues with WebGL 2.0 support' — advice unavailable on iOS, where every browser is Safari's engine.
detail: The one piece of good news is that the single-threaded export 'works very well on macOS and iOS too, where it always had compatibility issues with multiple threads exports'. Concretely an iPhone player gets: a multi-megabyte download; the WebGL 2.0 path Godot's own docs consider weakest; audio that will not start until they touch the screen; the game pausing whenever the tab is backgrounded because _process() stops; and no reliable fullscreen without an input event. The native iOS app stops being a nice-to-have after this move.

name: The web export has no threads by default, and threading code fails silently there
summary: Since 4.3 the default web build is single-threaded: WorkerThreadPool runs tasks inline inside add_task(), and Thread.start() is compiled to an empty body.
detail: Threaded web builds need SharedArrayBuffer and therefore Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin plus Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp; 4.3 added an 'Ensure Cross-Origin Isolation Headers' export option that injects them via a PWA service worker. On a non-threaded build main.cpp calls WorkerThreadPool::init(0, 0), and worker_thread_pool.cpp's _post_tasks falls back to processing on the calling thread when there are no workers — so add_task() runs the callable to completion before returning, and load_threaded_request() performs the whole load inside the request call. core/os/thread.h compiles start() to {} and is_started() to false without THREADS_ENABLED, so a script-level Thread.start() returns OK, never runs the function, and wait_to_finish() then errors. Guard with OS.has_feature("threads") — 'threads' and 'nothreads' are documented feature tags. Design rule: write the work so it is correct when it runs inline. Related: without threads the web build plays audio as Sample rather than Stream (audio/general/default_playback_type).

name: JavaScriptBridge.pwa_update() is a better freshCheck
summary: With PWA enabled the service worker reports a pending version through the pwa_update_available signal and pwa_needs_update(); pwa_update() applies it and reloads the app in every open tab.
detail: This maps one-to-one onto Cosmo's freshCheck() design and its guards — never swap during a live run, only from the menu — with the browser doing the detection instead of a range request over the game's own bundle plus a regex for a BUILD literal. The existing parser is doubly inert in the shipped Phaser build: externalLoop returns early, and minification destroys the const BUILD='…' form it matches anyway. PWA export options also give an Offline Page, icon sizes 144/180/512, orientation, display mode, and the cross-origin isolation header workaround.

name: WorkerThreadPool is Godot 4's default off-main-thread tool
summary: The pool exists at startup, so add_task/add_group_task cost nothing like creating a Thread; every task must still be waited for exactly once.
detail: add_task(action, high_priority=false, description="") and add_group_task(action, elements, tasks_needed=-1, high_priority=false, description="") — the group callable is invoked with 0..elements-1. wait_for_task_completion / wait_for_group_task_completion is what frees the task allocation, so it is required even after is_task_completed() returns true; calling it from inside another task can return ERR_BUSY. The docs warn the pool hurts if a task is not computationally expensive (rule of thumb: about a millisecond of real work per task). Godot 4.7's Using multiple threads manual page never mentions this class — the class reference is the only documentation.
